skill.name: layer-video
skill.description: Use when generating video with Layer: text-to-video, animating a still image, extending a clip, adding camera motion, generating native audio or lip sync, looping animations, or planning a multi-shot ad, trailer, or cutscene. Also when a video prompt produces the wrong motion or the shot drifts off the source image. Keywords: txt2vid, img2vid, image to video, camera motion, video effects, loop, seamless, trailer, cutscene, lipsync.
skill.summary: Plan Layer video generation with image anchors, motion prompts, capability filters, and cost checks.
skill.author: layerai

content.value_statement: Video prompts can produce weak motion, drifting subjects, or clips with the wrong duration. This skill guides Layer model selection, image anchoring, motion prompts, and loop checks.
actual_capabilities: Guide selection among text-to-video, image-to-video, clip extension, and video editing use cases.
Use approved still images as starting frames and supported ending frames to control appearance and shot endpoints.
Structure prompts around subject motion, camera movement, and motion rate.
Guide model filtering for fixed duration, native audio, lip sync, and loop capabilities.
Plan consistent multi-shot pieces and identify related skills for storyboarding and timeline assembly.
Outline generation estimates, approval, polling, and visual checks for a five-second animation loop.
limitations: Generation requires access to Layer tools and compatible models; this skill provides guidance rather than a standalone video engine.
Supported duration, audio, lip sync, camera effects, and frame inputs vary by model.
Image creation, storyboarding, timeline assembly, and general spending controls refer to separate skills.
Generation consumes credits and faces rate limits; visual continuity and seamless loops still require inspection.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Simple Motion Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Layer video prompt for a banner moving in wind. Specify subject motion, a locked camera, and movement rate.

prompt_templates.title: Animate an Approved Still
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan animation from my approved product still. Use a slow camera push and inspect supported frame inputs and structured camera effects.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Duration and Audio Capabilities
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Layer models for a six-second character dialogue clip with native audio and lip sync. Check duration support and estimate cost before generation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Shot Trailer
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a four-shot trailer from approved character art. Check single-generation feasibility, define motion per shot, and identify storyboard and assembly dependencies. Obtain cost approval.

output_examples.input: Plan a five-second idle loop from my approved character frame.
output: Select an image-to-video model with loop and fixed-duration capabilities.
Check whether the model accepts the same image as both starting and ending frames.
Motion prompt: The character breathes slowly while the cloak moves gently. Keep the camera locked and the motion continuous.
Estimate cost and request approval before generation when required.
Inspect playback across the clip boundary before accepting the result as a loop.

output_examples.input: Plan a three-shot product advertisement using approved still images.
output: Confirm whether one generation can support the intended advertisement before splitting it into shots.
Shot one: Show the product from the approved opening frame with a slow camera push.
Shot two: Use a compatible anchored frame for an orbit, checking structured camera-effect support.
Shot three: Hold the final product view with a locked camera.
If separate clips are required, use the related timeline skill for assembly and inspect continuity.

best_practices: Inspect the selected model schema before choosing frame inputs, camera effects, duration, or audio settings.
Anchor animation on approved images and specify subject motion, camera behavior, and movement rate.
Estimate spending before execution and inspect clip duration, appearance, and loop transitions after generation.
anti_patterns: Describe only a static scene or leave camera movement unspecified.
Assume every model supports exact duration, native audio, lip sync, or structured camera effects.
Call a clip seamless without inspecting the transition from its ending to its beginning.

faq.question: Does this skill generate videos by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides video workflows through Layer tools and models that must be available in your environment.

faq.question: Should I use text-to-video or image-to-video?
faq.answer: Use image-to-video when an approved still exists. Use text-to-video when you need to create the scene without an image anchor.

faq.question: Can I request an exact clip duration?
faq.answer: Filter for fixed-duration capability and verify the model supports your requested length. Some models ignore requested duration.

faq.question: Can videos include audio and lip sync?
faq.answer: Yes, when the selected model supports those capabilities. Native audio and lip sync require separate capability checks.

faq.question: How do I create a seamless loop?
faq.answer: Prefer a loop-capable model and naturally repeating motion. Where supported, reuse the image at both endpoints and inspect the playback transition.

faq.question: What additional skills are needed for a trailer?
faq.answer: The guidance references Layer image, art-direction, and video-timeline skills for image creation, storyboarding, and assembly. Missing skills require user installation.
